function: Learned SIC decoding order for weighted proportional-fairness utility in uplink NOMA, power by convex optimization: resource allocation, not symbol recovery or another of the seven areas; p. 1, p. 5
notes: Exclude, code function (first code that applies). The learned part is an attention-based actor network trained with REINFORCE with baseline. It maps user weights, maximum powers and channel gains to the SIC decoding order, and the power is then allocated by convex optimization (p. 5: 'X = {(wi, Pimax, gi)}i∈N, is fed into the actor network to generate the SIC ordering π'; 'we solve the subproblem P1 for the optimal power allocation p through convex optimization'; p. 7: 'interior-point method [56] of the CVX solver'). The objective and the metric are the network utility, a weighted sum of log Shannon rates (p. 4, problem P0; p. 11, Sec. 6.2 'Network Utility Performance'), and the index terms list 'resource allocation' (p. 1). This is NOMA resource allocation: the network does not take the received signal or recover symbols (area 1), estimate channels (area 2), or design precoders, beams or RIS (area 3), and the links are terrestrial, with no OTFS, ISAC, NTN or over-the-air FL. Codes 1 to 4 checked: a research article; a learned component makes a physical-layer decision; the SIC decoding order is a receiver decision, not in the above-PHY list. For the reviewer: area 1 could be weighed because SIC is multi-user detection and Sec. 5.1 adds a 2-antenna BS with MMSE equalization ('to detect symbols', p. 15). But the learned network only orders decoding for the rate utility, and no detection metric is reported. The main system has single-antenna users (p. 3) and a single-antenna BS ('Different from the single antenna scenario', p. 9). Identity: the PDF is arXiv:2407.14740v1 (p. 1), and Crossref lists the same title and authors for this DOI (IEEE Trans. Mobile Comput., Feb. 2025).
